name: Candor
definition: You willingly receive and give feedback; you are open about what's working and what needs to improve; you admit mistakes openly and share learnings widely.

rows.situation: Hearing something unflattering about your work
rows.under: Explains it away, or avoids the person who said it.
rows.justRight: Takes the feedback, asks one clarifying question, and changes the work where they are right.
rows.over: Treats every comment as an order and abandons your own judgment about the work.

rows.situation: A colleague's work that needs to improve
rows.under: Says it is fine, and the problem shows up later for someone else.
rows.justRight: Says what is working and what needs to change, to them, in time for them to use it.
rows.over: Delivers a running critique of the person, not the work, and calls that honesty.

rows.situation: A mistake you made that other people are still steering around
rows.under: Hopes it stays quiet, or mentions it only after someone else finds it.
rows.justRight: Says what you got wrong, what you learned, and what you are doing differently. Shares that beyond the people who already know.
rows.over: Turns the confession into the main event and never gets to the fix.

rows.situation: Talking about a colleague who is not in the room
rows.under: Says the sharp version to everyone except them.
rows.justRight: Says nothing about them that you have not said, or are not willing to say, to them.
rows.over: Refuses to brief your own manager on a real performance problem because the person is not in that meeting.

rows.situation: Feedback for someone more senior, or from a different background than yours
rows.under: Softens it into nothing because of the level or the distance.
rows.justRight: Says the same clear thing you would say to a peer, with enough care that they can hear it.
rows.over: Uses bluntness as a badge and ignores the effect on whether they can act on it.
